header:
Date: 2026-11-02 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Connor Lee (Redwood SE), Michael Chen (ApexCare CISO), Lina Gomez (ApexCare Head of Infra), Evan Park (ApexCare SRE), Sana Rao (ApexCare Compliance)
summary: Redwood walked ApexCare through SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning flow, discussed RBAC/least-privilege patterns, audit log retention and encryption/KMS options. ApexCare emphasized SOC2 needs, data residency for EU patients, and wanting strict role separation. Agreed to a hands-on RBAC workshop and test tenant provisioning.
topics: SSO/SAML setup, SCIM user provisioning, RBAC roles and least-privilege, audit logs and log retention, encryption and KMS integration, data residency (EU), SOC2/ISO evidence requests, next steps for pilot
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Rivera: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, i'll hand it to priya for the deep overview but mike thanks for taking time
[00:07] Michael Chen: thanks Alex, yeah want to be focused on SSO and how we'll map our roles we have pretty strict separation across infra and clinical apps
[00:15] Priya Shah: awesome, i'll start with the SSO flow, so Redwood supports SAML 2.0 IdPs, we also do SCIM v2 for user sync, typical flow is idp initiated or sp initiated auth, you can push groups via SCIM and map them to roles in the console
[00:30] Lina Gomez: quick q — can we do attribute-based provisioning? we want department and entitlements to come over
[00:36] Priya Shah: yes you can map attributes, there's an attribute mapping table, note sometimes the auto mapping gets noisy if IdP uses different claim names, we've seen that with azure ad and one really old okta tenant
[00:48] Evan Park: are we able to restrict admin access to a set of IP ranges? also curious about session timeout enforcement
[00:55] Connor Lee: we do support IP-based restrictions at the org and route level for Dedicated/private, sessions follow configurable SAML session timeouts and you can force re-auth via token TTLs
[01:06] Michael Chen: on SCIM, we need near real-time deprovisioning for terminated users, can't have lingering access
[01:12] Priya Shah: SCIM push is near real-time — typically sub minute for single user ops, bulk syncs are batched; we'll show you the webhook logs in the demo tenant
[01:22] Sana Rao: from compliance standpoint we need audit log integrity, tamper evidence and 12 month retention minimum, ideally immutable logs
[01:30] Alex Rivera: got it — Redwood's audit logs include actor, function, resource, and we'd provide signed export for compliance reviews; for immutability we integrate with your SIEM or S3 with WORM policies depending on deployment
[01:42] Michael Chen: encryption at rest — KMS integration? customer-managed keys?
[01:46] Priya Shah: yes we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in private deployments and for Dedicated we support bring-your-own-KMS for disk and object storage encryption; hosted supports Redwood-managed keys but we have envelope encryption and per-tenant key separation
[01:59] Lina Gomez: we need EU data residency for patient PII — can you guarantee processing in eu-west region?
[02:06] Alex Rivera: yes we have region pinning and routing policies; for private you can run control plane in your VPC, for hosted we can restrict region to eu-west only and ensure persistence in EU regions per contract
[02:16] Evan Park: speed question — we may need a low latency path for inference, does SSO affect latency on inference calls?
[02:24] Priya Shah: SSO only for control plane/auth; inference tokens are short-lived and cached at the edge, there shouldn't be a per-request SAML hop, token exchange happens once and then auth is via bearer tokens
[02:36] Michael Chen: RBAC — we have 6 roles today but prefer more granular, 'clinical reviewer' should only have read access to patient embeddings, not export or model revert
[02:45] Priya Shah: recommended pattern is least-privilege role templates: org-admin, infra-admin, svc-account, app-deployer, read-only, and clinical-reviewer; you can create custom roles with fine-grained permissions on route/model/actions
[02:59] Alex Rivera: we also support SCIM group sync to auto-assign roles, and SAML assertions can carry role claim so you can avoid manual mapping if your IdP supports it
[03:12] Sana Rao: auditability: can we get per-token and per-user token lineage? like who invoked what model and which route
[03:19] Priya Shah: yes logs include token id, user id, route, model version, request meta; we also have trace IDs you can correlate with your distributed tracing
[03:30] Michael Chen: what about tamper proofs — do you store checksums or sign logs
[03:33] Priya Shah: we provide signed log exports and support pushing to your SIEM, for private we can enable HSM signings on log batches, for hosted we can provide signed artifacts on request as part of the compliance pack
[03:48] Evan Park: SCIM: what about conflict resolution if someone changes role in both IdP and Redwood UI?
[03:53] Connor Lee: master is configurable — you can set IdP as source of truth or Redwood as source of truth, and there's a last-write-wins policy we can tune; we usually recommend IdP as source for org-managed accounts
[04:06] Priya Shah: another caveat — SCIM versions differ, some Okta tenants use custom schemas, we'll do a discovery sync to surface mismatches before cutover
[04:18] Michael Chen: can we have approver workflows for role elevation? security wants approval flow for any admin role grant
[04:24] Alex Rivera: Redwood doesn't ship a full approval workflow natively yet, but you can gate role changes through your IAM via SCIM and require an approval in IdP, or use webhooks to trigger your approval system; this is a known ask in roadmap for more native workflows
[04:40] Priya Shah: for immediate controls we recommend service accounts for automation, RBAC for human access and SCIM sync to control human role assignment; also use separate service principal for CI/CD deploys with minimal scopes
[04:55] Michael Chen: logging retention policy — is it configurable per customer?
[04:59] Priya Shah: yes, retention configurable by plan and deployment: hosted default 90 days, Dedicated can go to multi-year with archive to your S3, Private you control retention entirely in your infra
[05:11] Sana Rao: needs around SOC2 evidence — what artifacts will Redwood provide?
[05:15] Alex Rivera: we can provide SOC2 report, encryption diagrams, RBAC matrices, pen test summaries, and the audit log exports scoped to your account, plus a control mapping spreadsheet we fill out per request
[05:25] Michael Chen: for the pilot we want to test deprovisioning, role sync, and audit proofing, can we run a script-driven test to simulate 100 user churn events?
[05:32] Connor Lee: yes we'll help run churn tests in the sandbox tenant; SCIM bulk ops and webhook logs make it easy to validate deprovisioning scenarios
[05:44] Lina Gomez: network wise, for Dedicated we need to open specific peering rules, do you have a network checklist?
[05:50] Priya Shah: we'll send the VPC peering checklist; for private deployments you get more control and we provide a template with CIDR, ports, and cert fingerprints
[06:03] Alex Rivera: wanted to confirm scope — Are we ok to provision a test tenant scoped to EU region and run the RBAC workshop next week?
[06:10] Michael Chen: yes that's fine, we'll schedule the workshop, prefer Thurs but can be flexible
[06:16] Sana Rao: also please include the list of fields Redwood populates in audit events, we need to map to our control set
[06:22] Priya Shah: will do — we'll share the audit event schema, sample logs, and explain which fields are present (actor_id, actor_email, action, resource_type, resource_id, timestamp, trace_id)
[06:39] Evan Park: minor thing — SAML metadata rotation, can we automate key rollover without user disruption?
[06:43] Connor Lee: yes we have dual-key support for SAML metadata so you can publish new cert while old one still valid for overlap window, avoids outage during rollover
[06:55] Michael Chen: curious about service accounts — do they appear in audit logs as distinct actors?
[07:01] Priya Shah: yes service accounts have distinct actor ids and can be scoped to specific routes; we recommend naming conventions and ensure no broad admin privileges for svc accounts
[07:15] Alex Rivera: i'll recap — we'll send SSO & SCIM docs, RBAC templates, provision EU test tenant, schedule RBAC workshop, and run churn tests. any blockers?
[07:25] Michael Chen: none on our side, just need the compliance pack and the workshop invite
[07:30] Alex Rivera: great, thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and action items
[07:35] [call ends]
notes: There are a few transcription quirks (okta rendered as octa, KMS spelled sometimes as K-M-S), the team asked specifically for EU residency and a signed log export. Redwood to coordinate test tenant and workshop.
